_note: A person with severe disability (80% or more, s.127(9)(g)): "An individual, being resident in India, who is certified by a medical authority, at any time during the tax year, as a person with disability or person with severe disability, shall be allowed a deduction of ₹ 75000 or ₹ 125000, respectively" (s.154(1), p.185); the certificate furnished with the return (s.154(2)) — an entry condition; meanings from s.127 (s.154(3)). rulebook DED-80U-001. Old regime only (s.202(2)(a)(xii), p.227). TY 2026-27 and TY 2025-26; the 1961 counterpart, s.80U, is the TY 2025-26 version (W-075d3). D-138. TY 2025-26: Income-tax Act, 1961 s.80U(1) proviso (thc p.426): for a person with severe disability, "one hundred and twenty-five thousand rupees" — the same fixed row. sources/2026-10-07-chapter-via.md B18. D-146. In every regime as a row; the new regime forbids it through DIS-NEW-TAX-REGIME-NO-EXEMPTION, whose basis REG-NEW-TAX-REGIME-NO-EXEMPTION (S2 s.202(2)(a); 1961 s.115BAC(2)(i)) every explanation cites (D-166).

introducedBy.instrumentCitation: Income-tax Act, 1961 (43 of 1961), s.80U(1), proviso — subs. by Act 20 of 2015, s.24 (w.e.f. 1-4-2016)
